members.name: Identifier
members.doc:
A release version ("0.3.0") for an installed build, a GUID in braces for
a source tree — UE's EngineAssociation spelling, so a project names an
engine without naming a path that differs per machine.

types.name: FEngineRegistry
types.doc:
The per-user list of engines on this machine (<config>/InstalledEngines.ini,
[Installations] Identifier=Root) and the `.mproject` field that picks one.
MowoVersionSelector writes it; the project launcher and the shell verbs read
it. A file rather than the Windows registry so every OS shares one format.

members.name: List
members.doc:
Entries whose root no longer exists are left out (and kept on disk: an
unplugged drive is not an uninstall).

members.name: Register
members.doc:
Registers `root` and returns its identifier; a root already present keeps
the identifier it had, so projects that point at it stay valid.

members.name: EngineVersionAt
members.doc:
InstalledBuild.txt's EngineVersion for an installed build, else
Engine/EngineManifest.json's major.minor.patch.

members.name: ReadProjectAssociation
members.doc: `project.engineAssociation`, falling back to `project.engineVersion`.

members.name: WriteProjectAssociation
members.signature: static bool WriteProjectAssociation(const std::filesystem::path& projectFile, const std::string& identifier)

members.name: ResolveProjectEngineRoot
members.doc:
The registered engine the project names: by identifier, then by matching
version. Empty when none fits.

members.name: FindProgram
members.signature: static std::filesystem::path FindProgram(const std::filesystem::path& root, const std::vector<std::string>& baseNames)
members.doc:
The newest build of the named program under `root`, whatever layout made
it (Engine/Binaries/<Platform>, an installed build's Binaries/<Platform>,
or the older build/bin/<Config>). Empty when there is none.

members.name: FindBuildTool
members.doc: mbt.cmd / mbt.sh at the root of a source tree; empty for an installed build.

types.name: FLayerRegistry
types.doc:
Named layers, the single source of truth for every 32-bit layer mask in
the engine — camera culling masks, decal visibility, physics raycast
filters, audio occlusion. Layer 0..kBuiltinCount-1 ship with the engine
and cannot be renamed; the rest are project-defined and edited in
Project Settings > Layers.

The registry holds only the names. The masks themselves stay plain
uint32_t on the components, so runtime code never has to consult this.

members.name: GetNames
members.doc: Always kMaxLayers entries; empty string = undefined slot.

members.name: GetDisplayName
members.doc:
Name if the slot is defined, "Layer <n>" otherwise. Never empty, so
the UI always has something to draw.

members.name: FindIndex
members.doc: -1 when no slot carries the name. Case-sensitive.

members.name: SetName
members.signature: bool SetName(int32_t index, const std::string& name)
members.doc: Rejects built-in slots, out-of-range indices and duplicates.

members.name: Apply
members.doc:
Replaces every user slot at once. Entries beyond kMaxLayers are
dropped, built-in slots are restored regardless of what came in.

members.name: MaskContains
members.signature: static bool MaskContains(uint32_t mask, int32_t index)

members.name: Summarize
members.doc:
"All", "None", "Default", "Default, Water", "3 Layers" — the closed
state of the inspector's layer-mask dropdown. Bits pointing at
undefined slots still count, so a mask never silently reads as None.

members.name: Monolithic
members.doc:
On by default, as `mbt package` is for Shipping: a modular Shipping
package ships ~45 first-party DLLs that ThinLTO cannot optimise across.

members.name: TargetPlatforms
members.doc:
The platforms the project targets, comma separated in the packaged
layouts' folder names ("Win64,Linux"). The launcher's new-project
wizard writes them, the Packaging window shows and edits them, and
`mbt package` warns when it packages for a platform not listed. Empty
means this host.

members.name: PackageOutputDir
members.doc: Stored form — see ToStoredPath. Empty means "the default".

members.name: DefaultPackageOutputDir
members.doc:
"Saved/Packaged/<Product>" and "Saved/Cooked" — nothing a fresh
project writes names a machine.

members.name: Load
members.doc:
False when there is no file yet; the struct then holds the defaults.
A legacy absolute value inside the project comes back relativised.

members.name: ToStoredPath
members.signature: static std::string ToStoredPath(const Project& project, const std::string& path)
members.doc:
Absolute inside the project → project-relative, forward slashes. A
relative path is normalised. Absolute outside the project → unchanged
(generic form) plus a one-time warning.

members.name: ToAbsolutePath
members.signature: static std::string ToAbsolutePath(const Project& project, const std::string& stored)
members.doc: The inverse: a stored value → the directory on this machine.

members.name: CanonicalPlatformName
members.doc:
"windows", "win64" → "Win64"; "mac", "macos" → "Mac"; anything else
keeps its spelling with the first letter upper-cased ("linux" →
"Linux"), so a hand-edited file and the wizard name a platform alike.

members.name: TargetPlatformList
members.doc: The list as written, canonical, without duplicates; {host} when empty.

members.name: TargetsPlatform
members.signature: bool TargetsPlatform(const std::string& platform, const std::string& host) const

members.name: SetTargetsPlatform
members.signature: void SetTargetsPlatform(const std::string& platform, bool targeted, const std::string& host)
members.doc:
Adds or removes one platform and keeps the others as they were. The
last one is never removed: an empty list means "this host", which
would quietly re-target the platform the user just turned off.

members.name: Icon
members.doc:
Lucide icon name ("scan", "gamepad", ...) shown by the plugin
manager; empty falls back to a category glyph.

members.name: EngineVersion
members.doc:
"major.minor" of the engine the plugin was made for. Empty = unstated,
which loads as before; a stated version that differs blocks the plugin
instead of letting it register structs of a layout this engine does
not have.

members.name: bRequiresOnline
members.doc:
Read by the build side (monolithic NoOnline link, server staging, DLC
packaging). Carried here so a manifest saved back through
SaveDescriptor keeps them — the writer used to drop all three.

members.name: bBeta
members.doc: UE's IsBetaVersion: the Plugins window marks it "beta".

members.name: MarketplaceUrl
BlockedReason
members.doc:
Why an ENABLED plugin still does not load: a dependency that is not
installed, is disabled, cannot load itself, or closes a cycle. Empty
when nothing stands in the way. A blocked plugin mounts no content and
loads no modules — it would come up half-wired otherwise.

types.name: FPluginContentMount
types.doc:
One live content mount. MountPoint is the VFS prefix ("Plugins/<Name>")
that asset references serialize as; ContentDir is the canonical disk
directory it resolves to.

members.name: LoadDescriptor
members.signature: static bool LoadDescriptor(const std::filesystem::path& manifestPath, FPluginDescriptor& outDescriptor, std::string* outError = nullptr)

members.name: SaveDescriptor
members.signature: static bool SaveDescriptor(const std::filesystem::path& manifestPath, const FPluginDescriptor& descriptor)

members.name: SetEnginePluginsDirOverride
members.doc:
Points engine-plugin discovery at another tree; empty restores Engine/Plugins.
Tests use it to exercise the engine tier against a fixture plugin, since the
plugins the engine ships are free to change what they carry.

members.name: SetLoadsEditorModules
members.doc:
Whether this host loads plugin modules declared `"type": "Editor"`. Only
the editor turns it on, before engine init: such a module links the
editor framework, which a player or a server does not ship, and the type
field was parsed and ignored until this existed.

members.name: LoadEnginePlugins
members.doc:
Discover, mount and load the engine-tier plugins under Engine/Plugins.
Runs once at engine init, independent of any project — idempotent.

members.name: LoadPackagedPlugins
members.doc:
A packaged game has no plugin folders: its plugin DLLs sit beside the host
exe and the enabled plugins' manifests travel as one JSON array in the
engine pak (Plugins.json). Registers each as an enabled engine plugin and
loads its modules in dependency order; content is already in the paks.

members.name: Unmount
members.doc:
Tears down project plugins only; engine plugins stay live across
project open/close.

members.name: UnmountAll
members.doc: Full teardown including engine plugins — for engine shutdown.

members.name: FindPlugin
members.signature: const FPluginInfo* FindPlugin(const std::string& name) const

members.name: SetEnabled
members.signature: bool SetEnabled(const std::string& name, bool enabled)

members.name: DisabledDependenciesOf
members.doc:
Installed plugins `name` needs, directly or through another dependency,
that are disabled right now — what enabling it has to enable too.

members.name: EnabledDependentsOf
members.doc: Enabled plugins that stop loading if `name` is disabled.

members.name: ResolveDependencies
members.doc:
Recomputes every plugin's BlockedReason. Pure over the plugin list, so
callers that only change state run it and then apply mounts.

members.name: EngineVersionString
members.doc: "major.minor" of this engine, the form a manifest's engineVersion takes.

members.name: EngineVersionMismatch
members.doc:
Empty when a manifest's stated engine version is compatible (or not
stated); otherwise the reason, in BlockedReason's phrasing. Patch
releases do not break plugins, so only major.minor is compared.

members.name: GetContentMounts
members.doc:
Snapshot of the live content mounts. Copied out because callers read
it from worker threads while the main thread may mount or unmount.

members.name: ContentRevision
members.doc:
Bumped on every mount/unmount. Anything that caches a view of plugin
content (asset registry, content browser) polls this instead of
subscribing to a delegate.

members.name: ToPluginVfsPath
members.signature: static bool ToPluginVfsPath(const std::string& absolutePath, std::string& outVfsPath)
members.doc:
Absolute disk path → "Plugins/<Name>/..." when the path sits under a
mounted plugin's Content directory.

members.name: ResolvePluginVfsPath
members.doc:
"Plugins/<Name>/..." → absolute disk path. Empty when the plugin is
not mounted or the path is not a plugin path.

types.name: ProjectScriptingSettings
types.doc:
Dead C# residue — the managed scripting layer was removed. Still
serialized for manifest compatibility; do not add fields.

types.name: ProjectLobbyType
types.doc:
Default visibility for platform lobbies. Mirrors
Networking's EPlatformLobbyType (Project sits below Networking's
consumers and must not include its headers).

types.name: ProjectPlatformSettings
types.doc:
Platform/social integration (Steam + Discord). Steam and Discord
only initialize when explicitly enabled here with a non-zero id.

members.name: mowoOnlineEnabled
members.doc:
Mowo Online Services (MowoOnlinePlatform plugin): the Mowo ID product
id the Mowo Games Launcher knows the game by, and whether a start
outside the launcher re-launches through it (MOS_RestartAppIfNecessary).

members.name: presenceDetailsFormat
members.doc: Rich-presence format strings with {details} / {state} tokens.

members.name: iconPath
members.doc: Absolute path to .ico/.png file

types.name: ProjectLayerSettings
types.doc:
User-defined layer names, index-aligned with FLayerRegistry (slot 0..4 are
the engine's built-ins and are re-imposed on load, whatever the manifest
says). Stored on the settings so the manifest round-trip stays in one place.

types.name: FEditorUserState
types.doc:
Per-project editor state persisted to Saved/Config/Editor/UserPreferences.json
(user-local, gitignored). Not part of the committed .mproject manifest — it
carries the last viewport camera and the set of open asset-editor documents
so a reopen lands the user where they left off. Robust to missing/stale entries.

members.name: openDocuments
members.doc: Each entry is "editorType|path" for an open asset-editor document.

members.name: favoriteAssets
members.doc: Content-browser favorites — asset paths the user starred.

members.name: favoriteFolders
members.doc:
Content-browser favourite folders, listed under FAVOURITES in the
Sources panel.

members.name: folderColors
members.doc:
Content-browser folder tints, "path|#RRGGBB" per entry (UE5 folder
colors). Absent = the default untinted folder.

members.name: savedColors
members.doc:
Colour-picker saved swatches, "#RRGGBBAA" per entry — the palette is
process-wide in Arc, this is its per-project persistence.

members.name: panelInstances
members.doc:
Extra dock-panel instances (a second Content Browser, a third Details),
"<tabId>|<panel state>" per entry. The layout file already restores the
TABS by id; this is what makes a restored instance come back looking at
what it was looking at instead of at defaults. The state half is opaque
here — each panel owns its own encoding.

members.name: recentScenes
members.doc:
Recently opened scenes, most recent first, "<pin>|<path>" per entry where
<pin> is 0 or 1. Pinned entries survive eviction, which is the whole
reason the flag is stored next to the path instead of in a second list.

members.name: previewSceneSettings
members.doc:
Preview Scene Settings per asset-editor kind, "<kind>|<encoded rig>" per
entry — the lighting, floor, grid and post an artist set for the static
mesh editor, the skeletal mesh editor and so on. Keyed by KIND and not by
asset on purpose: it is a editor preference, and re-making the same
three-point rig for every mesh is the thing it exists to stop. The value
half is opaque here; FPreviewSceneSettingsDrawer owns its encoding.

members.name: editorPreferences
members.doc:
Editor Preferences, "<key>=<value>" per entry. Per user and per project
like UE's EditorPerProjectUserSettings; the editor owns the keys, and an
entry it no longer knows is dropped on the next save.

members.name: kMaxRecentScenes
members.doc:
Ten unpinned rows is roughly a File menu's worth; pins ride above the cap
so a pinned set larger than this cannot silently lose its last member.

members.name: MakeRecentScene
members.signature: static std::string MakeRecentScene(const std::string& path, bool pinned)

members.name: PushRecentScene
members.signature: static void PushRecentScene(std::vector<std::string>& entries, const std::string& path)

members.name: RemoveRecentScene
members.signature: static void RemoveRecentScene(std::vector<std::string>& entries, const std::string& path)

members.name: ToggleRecentScenePin
members.signature: static void ToggleRecentScenePin(std::vector<std::string>& entries, const std::string& path)

members.name: gameModeClass
members.doc:
MCLASS name of the game mode to spawn when the start scene
begins play ("AGameMode" or a game subclass). Empty = no game
framework (legacy/sandbox projects).

members.name: created
members.doc: ISO 8601 timestamp

members.name: modified
members.doc: ISO 8601 timestamp

members.name: assetFormat
members.doc:
1 = text assets without a package summary; 2 = packages (each type
under its own extension, .mmap levels with .actor files), kept migrated
on every open. See FAssetPackageMigration.

members.name: modGame
members.doc:
A mod project names the game it modifies (its .mproject, relative to
the mod root or absolute). Empty for a game.

members.name: SetEditorConfigPath
members.doc:
Points the per-user editor state somewhere other than Saved/Config/Editor
— the host's scratch directory while user config is ignored.

members.name: EnsureDerivedDirectories
members.doc:
Create the disposable trees (Intermediate/*, Saved/*) if missing.
Idempotent — runs on every project open.

members.name: ToProjectRelativePath
members.doc:
Absolute filesystem path → project-relative, e.g. "Content/Models/char.fbx".
Idempotent for a path that is already project-relative. A path that
climbs out of the working directory ("../../Samples/SampleProject/Content/x")
is anchored against the CWD first — it is relative to the shell, not to
the project, and storing it verbatim made it unresolvable from anywhere
else.

members.name: StartsWithParentSegment
members.doc:
True for a path whose FIRST segment is "..". Such a path is relative to
the working directory and can never be project-relative, so it is the
one relative form that still has to be anchored before use.

members.name: SetBaseGameRoot
members.doc:
A mod project sees the game's own tree beneath its own: a project-
relative path resolves to the mod's file when the mod has one and to
the game's otherwise, and an absolute path inside the game maps back to
the same "Content/..." key. The game's files are never written —
ToWritableAbsolutePath always names the mod's copy.

members.name: migrated
members.doc: false + ok = nothing to do

members.name: NeedsMigration
members.doc: True when either upgrade below has work to do.

members.name: NeedsLayoutMigration
members.doc:
True when the project root carries the old layout: an Assets/ dir
and no Content/ dir. A root with both is treated as already
migrated (Content/ wins) and left alone.

members.name: NeedsUserStateMigration
members.doc: True while the retired .mowo/ directory is still there.

members.name: NeedsReferenceRewrite
members.doc:
True while a layout migration has moved Assets/ but not yet rewritten
every reference to it — the state an interrupted or failed rewrite
leaves, which nothing else on disk records once Content/ exists.

members.name: Migrate
members.doc:
Migrate in place. Idempotent: a no-op (ok, !migrated) on a project
that is already in the new layout.

members.name: RewriteAssetReferences
members.doc:
Rewrite "Assets/..." → "Content/..." inside one text file. Public
for the self-test; Migrate walks the tree and calls this. Returns the
references rewritten, 0 when there were none or the file could not be
read or replaced.

members.name: TryRewriteAssetReferences
members.signature: static bool TryRewriteAssetReferences(const std::filesystem::path& file, uint32_t& outRewritten)
members.doc:
Same, telling "nothing to rewrite" apart from "could not rewrite". The
file is replaced through a temp file, never truncated in place.

members.name: IsRewritableFile
members.doc:
True for the text formats that can carry asset references: every text
asset, level and sidecar type of the file-type table, canonical or
legacy (.mat/.mdfmat, .mmap/.mdfscene, .mdfmeta, .mdf, .mproject, ...).

members.name: RefreshGitAttributes
members.doc:
Brings the file-type block of <project>/.gitattributes up to date with
the table (FFileTypes::GitAttributesBlock). Only a file that already
carries the block's markers is touched — the block is the engine's, the
rest of the file and a file without markers are the team's. True when
the file was rewritten. Cheap enough to run on every open.

members.name: lastOpened
members.doc: ISO 8601 timestamp

types.name: RecentProjects
types.doc: Stored in the platform-specific user data directory.

members.name: AddProject
members.signature: void AddProject(const std::string& name, const std::filesystem::path& projectFilePath)
members.doc: Moves the project to the front if it is already present.

members.name: MAX_RECENT_PROJECTS
members.doc: Maximum number of recent projects to store
